clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old male presented with a 4-month history of right eye pain, tearing, photophobia, and decreased vision following ocular trauma with a vegetal corneal foreign body. Initial treatment with topical antibiotics was ineffective, and the diagnosis was reconsidered to metaherpetic keratitis with antiviral therapy initiated. On presentation to our clinic, slit-lamp examination revealed a characteristic peripheral, crescent-shaped corneal ulcer located 2 mm from the limbus, extending 180° inferiorly and nasally (7:00-1:00 o'clock position), with epithelial and superficial stromal involvement, conjunctival blood vessel invasion at the ulcer margin, and normal corneal sensitivity. The left eye was unaffected. Comprehensive workup including blood investigations, serology (hepatitis C, syphilis), immunological markers (rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, ANA, pANCA, cANCA, anti-Ro, anti-La), urinary analysis, and corneal culture were all negative, ruling out infectious and systemic causes. Critically, the ulcer demonstrated progressive aggravation with central migration, further advancement of corneal blood vessels, and increased astigmatism (+2.75/-2.50/85°) despite antiviral therapy—this progressive stromal melting despite appropriate antimicrobial treatment is the defining pathophysiological feature of Mooren's ulcer. Topical steroids (5 times daily) were initiated with adjunctive topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor and beta-blocker for intraocular pressure control. final.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old male presented with a 4-month history of right eye pain, tearing, photophobia, and decreased vision following ocular trauma with a vegetal corneal foreign body. Initial treatment with topical antibiotics was ineffective, and the diagnosis was reconsidered to metaherpetic keratitis with antiviral therapy initiated. Topical steroids (5 times daily) were initiated with adjunctive topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor and beta-blocker for intraocular pressure control. At 5-day follow-up, significant improvement was documented with complete regression of corneal blood vessels, shallow ulcer with only central fluorescein staining, improved visual acuity (0.3 with best correction), and decreased astigmatism (+1.75/-1.75/83°). At 1-month follow-up, complete epithelial closure was achieved with visual acuity restored to 0.5 with best correction (baseline pre-ulcer vision), intraocular pressure 18 mmHg, and further reduction in corneal astigmatism (+1.25/-1.25/78°).
